- changelog.d/4723-require-plan-run-id.md | Line or code reference: line 19 ("For contributors" paragraph)
  Problem: The contributor-note sentence "tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_plan_polling_guard.py runs the real step scripts against a stubbed gh to cover the missing-ID, later-page, other-issue, page-cap, and unreadable-page cases for all three captures" does not list the empty-ISSUE_TITLE case covered by `test_clarify_and_implement_fail_before_polling_without_an_issue_title` (the round-1 finding). The PR description's "Files" and "Checks run" sections also still say "6 behavioural tests" and "6 of 6 fail" even though the file ships 7 (the seventh is the new empty-title guard test). This is a doc-only drift between the originally-listed deliverables and the round-1 commit that addressed AD-9.
  Why it fails at runtime: This is a documentation issue, not a runtime defect. A future reviewer auditing the contract from the changelog would undercount the test surface.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml | Line or code reference: 632-636 (wait-clarify) and 1134-1138 (wait-implement)
  Issue: The empty-title guard uses `[ -z "${ISSUE_TITLE}" ]`, which treats unset and empty as the same. The env block above sources the title from `${{ steps.create-issue.outputs.title }}`, so a whitespace-only title (e.g. from a future caller that supplies a title with leading/trailing spaces) would pass the guard and reach the `display_title == $title` filter, which would still match a run whose `display_title` is exactly that whitespace. The wait-plan guard at lines 799-803 has the same property, so this is a parity issue, not a regression.
  Suggested minimal fix: tighten the guard to reject whitespace-only titles by trimming before the test, e.g. `if [ -z "${ISSUE_TITLE// /}" ]; then` (parameter expansion removes all spaces; tabs would still pass). Five lines per step if applied in both places; matches the spirit of the AD-9 reasoning.
  Estimated lines changed: 4 (2 lines per step × 2 steps)
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
